newsitem.title: USA: Colorado cty appeals Moody's muni antitrust ruling.
newsitem.headline: Colorado cty appeals Moody's muni antitrust ruling.

text.p: Colorado's largest school district appealed a U.S. judge's dismissal of federal antitrust claims that the locality filed against Moody's Investors Service Inc., a lawyer for the school district said Thursday.
"We think the judge erred," Stuart Stuller, lawyer for Jefferson County School District, said in a telephone interview. "His ruling is an unprecedented extension of current law."
The school district last year charged that Moody's violated U.S. antitrust laws and state statutes in 1993 by pressuring the school district to hire the firm to rate millions of dollars of debt.

U.S. District Judge William Downes on April 8 dismissed the charges saying that it would be a "calamity" to "muzzle into silence" bond rating firms by applying the Sherman Antitrust Act to their rating activities.
But Stuller on Thursday said the kind of "predatory conduct" that Moody's engaged in is "not protected by the First Amendment."
Moody's attorney Robert Callagy, a partner with Satterlee Stephens Burke & Burke, responded: "We'll deal with this. We feel Judge Downes' decision is correct and well reasoned."
